_doc: The narrator. Plain speech, short sentences, no fake-epic vocabulary, no translation register. The test line is 'He said no.' - three level words. If a line could not be said aloud to a friend, it is written wrong. Speaker attribution survives everywhere: a statement by a character is never rendered as narrator fact.

voice_settings.rule: High stability on purpose. Low stability lets the model perform, and the direction forbids performance. If a read sounds performed, the settings or the voice are wrong - do not fix it by rewriting the line.

per_line_rule: Lines are generated one at a time, never the whole script in one call. The edit owns the silences, not the model.

M3.overall: A room where something is being refused. The narrator does not plead and does not judge. Level.

lines.03-05: Flat. The king is standing; do not announce it.
lines.03-09: This is Dasaratha's statement, not ours. Attribute it in the read - a shade of quotation, not an impersonation.
lines.05-06: The staff strike. Say nothing over it. The line before ends clean and the line after starts late.
lines.07-02: 'He said no.' Three level words. No fall on 'no'. Do not land it.

en.register: plain modern English. No archaism, no 'thee', no inversion.

hi.register: plain spoken Hindi. Not Sanskritised, not Urdu-leaning. The register of speech, not of recitation.

te.register: plain spoken Telugu. Not grandhika. The register of speech.
